requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that entities falling within the scope of this Directive and, where
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that entities falling within the scope of this Directive and, where relevant, other entities not falling within the scope of this Directive are able to exchange on a voluntary basis relevant cybersecurity information among themselves, including information relating to cyber threats, near misses, vulnerabilities, techniques and procedures, indicators of compromise, adversarial tactics, threat-actor-specific information, cybersecurity alerts and recommendations regarding configuration of cybersecurity tools to detect cyberattacks, where such information sharing:

requirements.title: Aims to prevent, detect, respond to or recover from incidents or to mitigate their impact
requirements.text: aims to prevent, detect, respond to or recover from incidents or to mitigate their impact;

requirements.title: Enhances the level of cybersecurity, in particular through raising awareness in relation to
requirements.text: enhances the level of cybersecurity, in particular through raising awareness in relation to cyber threats, limiting or impeding the ability of such threats to spread, supporting a range of defensive capabilities, vulnerability remediation and disclosure, threat detection, containment and prevention techniques, mitigation strategies, or response and recovery stages or promoting collaborative cyber threat research between public and private entities.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the exchange of information takes place within communities of
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the exchange of information takes place within communities of essential and important entities, and where relevant, their suppliers or service providers. Such exchange shall be implemented through cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements in respect of the potentially sensitive nature of the information shared.

requirements.title: Member States shall facilitate the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing
requirements.text: Member States shall facilitate the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article. Such arrangements may specify operational elements, including the use of dedicated ICT platforms and automation tools, content and conditions of the information-sharing arrangements. In laying down the details of the involvement of public authorities in such arrangements, Member States may impose conditions on the information made available by the competent authorities or the CSIRTs. Member States shall offer assistance for the application of such arrangements in accordance with their policies referred to in Article 7(2), point (h).

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities notify the competent
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities notify the competent authorities of their participation in the cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements referred to in paragraph 2, upon entering into such arrangements, or, as applicable, of their withdrawal from such arrangements, once the withdrawal takes effect.

requirements.title: ENISA shall provide assistance for the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing
requirements.text: ENISA shall provide assistance for the establishment of cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements referred to in paragraph 2 by exchanging best practices and providing guidance.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that, in addition to the notification obligation provided for in
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that, in addition to the notification obligation provided for in Article 23, notifications can be submitted to the CSIRTs or, where applicable, the competent authorities, on a voluntary basis, by:

requirements.title: Essential and important entities with regard to incidents, cyber threats and near misses
requirements.text: essential and important entities with regard to incidents, cyber threats and near misses;

requirements.title: Entities other than those referred to in point (a), regardless of whether they fall within the
requirements.text: entities other than those referred to in point (a), regardless of whether they fall within the scope of this Directive, with regard to significant incidents, cyber threats and near misses.

requirements.title: Member States shall process the notifications referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article in
requirements.text: Member States shall process the notifications referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 23. Member States may prioritise the processing of mandatory notifications over voluntary notifications. Where necessary, the CSIRTs and, where applicable, the competent authorities shall provide the single points of contact with the information about notifications received pursuant to this Article, while ensuring the confidentiality and appropriate protection of the information provided by the notifying entity. Without prejudice to the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, voluntary reporting shall not result in the imposition of any additional obligations upon the notifying entity to which it would not have been subject had it not submitted the notification.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities effectively supervise and take the
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities effectively supervise and take the measures necessary to ensure compliance with this Directive.

requirements.title: Member States may allow their competent authorities to prioritise supervisory tasks
requirements.text: Member States may allow their competent authorities to prioritise supervisory tasks. Such prioritisation shall be based on a risk-based approach. To that end, when exercising their supervisory tasks provided for in Articles 32 and 33, the competent authorities may establish supervisory methodologies allowing for a prioritisation of such tasks following a risk-based approach.

requirements.title: The competent authorities shall work in close cooperation with supervisory authorities under
requirements.text: The competent authorities shall work in close cooperation with supervisory authorities under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 when addressing incidents resulting in personal data breaches, without prejudice to the competence and tasks of the supervisory authorities under that Regulation.

requirements.title: Without prejudice to national legislative and institutional frameworks, Member States shall
requirements.text: Without prejudice to national legislative and institutional frameworks, Member States shall ensure that, in the supervision of compliance of public administration entities with this Directive and the imposition of enforcement measures with regard to infringements of this Directive, the competent authorities have appropriate powers to carry out such tasks with operational independence vis-à-vis the public administration entities supervised. Member States may decide on the imposition of appropriate, proportionate and effective supervisory and enforcement measures in relation to those entities in accordance with the national legislative and institutional frameworks.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the supervisory or enforcement measures imposed on essential
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the supervisory or enforcement measures imposed on essential entities in respect of the obligations laid down in this Directive are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, taking into account the circumstances of each individual case.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their supervisory
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their supervisory tasks in relation to essential entities, have the power to subject those entities at least to:

requirements.title: On-site inspections and off-site supervision, including random checks conducted by trained
requirements.text: on-site inspections and off-site supervision, including random checks conducted by trained professionals;

requirements.title: Regular and targeted security audits carried out by an independent body or a competent authority
requirements.text: regular and targeted security audits carried out by an independent body or a competent authority;

requirements.title: Ad hoc audits, including where justified on the ground of a significant incident or an
requirements.text: ad hoc audits, including where justified on the ground of a significant incident or an infringement of this Directive by the essential entity;

requirements.title: Security scans based on objective, non-discriminatory, fair and transparent risk assessment
requirements.text: security scans based on objective, non-discriminatory, fair and transparent risk assessment criteria, where necessary with the cooperation of the entity concerned;

requirements.title: Requests for information necessary to assess the cybersecurity risk-management measures adopted
requirements.text: requests for information necessary to assess the cybersecurity risk-management measures adopted by the entity concerned, including documented cybersecurity policies, as well as compliance with the obligation to submit information to the competent authorities pursuant to Article 27;

requirements.title: Requests to access data, documents and information necessary to carry out their supervisory
requirements.text: requests to access data, documents and information necessary to carry out their supervisory tasks;

requirements.title: Requests for evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies, such as the results of
requirements.text: requests for evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies, such as the results of security audits carried out by a qualified auditor and the respective underlying evidence. The targeted security audits referred to in the first subparagraph, point (b), shall be based on risk assessments conducted by the competent authority or the audited entity, or on other risk-related available information. The results of any targeted security audit shall be made available to the competent authority. The costs of such targeted security audit carried out by an independent body shall be paid by the audited entity, except in duly substantiated cases when the competent authority decides otherwise.

requirements.title: When exercising their powers under paragraph 2, point (e), (f) or (g), the competent authorities
requirements.text: When exercising their powers under paragraph 2, point (e), (f) or (g), the competent authorities shall state the purpose of the request and specify the information requested.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities, when exercising their enforcement
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities, when exercising their enforcement powers in relation to essential entities, have the power at least to:

requirements.title: Issue warnings about infringements of this Directive by the entities concerned
requirements.text: issue warnings about infringements of this Directive by the entities concerned;

requirements.title: Adopt binding instructions, including with regard to measures necessary to prevent or remedy an
requirements.text: adopt binding instructions, including with regard to measures necessary to prevent or remedy an incident, as well as time-limits for the implementation of such measures and for reporting on their implementation, or an order requiring the entities concerned to remedy the deficiencies identified or the infringements of this Directive;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to cease conduct that infringes this Directive and desist from
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to cease conduct that infringes this Directive and desist from repeating that conduct;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to ensure that their cybersecurity risk-management measures comply
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to ensure that their cybersecurity risk-management measures comply with Article 21 or to fulfil the reporting obligations laid down in Article 23, in a specified manner and within a specified period;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to inform the natural or legal persons with regard to which they
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to inform the natural or legal persons with regard to which they provide services or carry out activities which are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat of the nature of the threat, as well as of any possible protective or remedial measures which can be taken by those natural or legal persons in response to that threat;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to implement the recommendations provided as a result of a security
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to implement the recommendations provided as a result of a security audit within a reasonable deadline;

requirements.title: Designate a monitoring officer with well-defined tasks for a determined period of time to
requirements.text: designate a monitoring officer with well-defined tasks for a determined period of time to oversee the compliance of the entities concerned with Articles 21 and 23;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to make public aspects of infringements of this Directive in a
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to make public aspects of infringements of this Directive in a specified manner;

requirements.title: Impose, or request the imposition by the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance
requirements.text: impose, or request the imposition by the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance with national law, of an administrative fine pursuant to Article 34 in addition to any of the measures referred to in points (a) to (h) of this paragraph.

requirements.title: Where enforcement measures adopted pursuant to paragraph 4, points (a) to (d) and (f), are
requirements.text: Where enforcement measures adopted pursuant to paragraph 4, points (a) to (d) and (f), are ineffective, Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities have the power to establish a deadline by which the essential entity is requested to take the necessary action to remedy the deficiencies or to comply with the requirements of those authorities. If the requested action is not taken within the deadline set, Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities have the power to:

requirements.title: Suspend temporarily, or request a certification or authorisation body, or a court or tribunal
requirements.text: suspend temporarily, or request a certification or authorisation body, or a court or tribunal, in accordance with national law, to suspend temporarily a certification or authorisation concerning part or all of the relevant services provided or activities carried out by the essential entity;

requirements.title: Request that the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance with national law, prohibit
requirements.text: request that the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance with national law, prohibit temporarily any natural person who is responsible for discharging managerial responsibilities at chief executive officer or legal representative level in the essential entity from exercising managerial functions in that entity. Temporary suspensions or prohibitions imposed pursuant to this paragraph shall be applied only until the entity concerned takes the necessary action to remedy the deficiencies or comply with the requirements of the competent authority for which such enforcement measures were applied. The imposition of such temporary suspensions or prohibitions shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with the general principles of Union law and the Charter, including the right to an effective remedy and to a fair trial, the presumption of innocence and the rights of the defence. The enforcement measures provided for in this paragraph shall not be applicable to public administration entities that are subject to this Directive.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that any natural person responsible for or acting as a legal
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that any natural person responsible for or acting as a legal representative of an essential entity on the basis of the power to represent it, the authority to take decisions on its behalf or the authority to exercise control of it has the power to ensure its compliance with this Directive. Member States shall ensure that it is possible to hold such natural persons liable for breach of their duties to ensure compliance with this Directive. As regards public administration entities, this paragraph shall be without prejudice to national law as regards the liability of public servants and elected or appointed officials.

requirements.title: When taking any of the enforcement measures referred to in paragraph 4 or 5, the competent
requirements.text: When taking any of the enforcement measures referred to in paragraph 4 or 5, the competent authorities shall comply with the rights of the defence and take account of the circumstances of each individual case and, as a minimum, take due account of:

requirements.title: The seriousness of the infringement and the importance of the provisions breached, the
requirements.text: the seriousness of the infringement and the importance of the provisions breached, the following, inter alia, constituting serious infringement in any event:

requirements.title: Repeated violations
requirements.text: repeated violations; (ii) a failure to notify or remedy significant incidents; (iii) a failure to remedy deficiencies following binding instructions from competent authorities; (iv) the obstruction of audits or monitoring activities ordered by the competent authority following the finding of an infringement;

requirements.title: Providing false or grossly inaccurate information in relation to cybersecurity risk-management
requirements.text: providing false or grossly inaccurate information in relation to cybersecurity risk-management measures or reporting obligations laid down in Articles 21 and 23;

requirements.title: The duration of the infringement
requirements.text: the duration of the infringement;

requirements.title: Any relevant previous infringements by the entity concerned
requirements.text: any relevant previous infringements by the entity concerned;

requirements.title: Any material or non-material damage caused, including any financial or economic loss, effects on
requirements.text: any material or non-material damage caused, including any financial or economic loss, effects on other services and the number of users affected;

requirements.title: Any intent or negligence on the part of the perpetrator of the infringement
requirements.text: any intent or negligence on the part of the perpetrator of the infringement;

requirements.title: Any measures taken by the entity to prevent or mitigate the material or non-material damage
requirements.text: any measures taken by the entity to prevent or mitigate the material or non-material damage;

requirements.title: Any adherence to approved codes of conduct or approved certification mechanisms
requirements.text: any adherence to approved codes of conduct or approved certification mechanisms;

requirements.title: The level of cooperation of the natural or legal persons held responsible with the competent
requirements.text: the level of cooperation of the natural or legal persons held responsible with the competent authorities.

requirements.title: The competent authorities shall set out a detailed reasoning for their enforcement measures
requirements.text: The competent authorities shall set out a detailed reasoning for their enforcement measures. Before adopting such measures, the competent authorities shall notify the entities concerned of their preliminary findings. They shall also allow a reasonable time for those entities to submit observations, except in duly substantiated cases where immediate action to prevent or respond to incidents would otherwise be impeded.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive inform the
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive inform the relevant competent authorities within the same Member State under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 when exercising their supervisory and enforcement powers aiming to ensure compliance of an entity identified as a critical entity under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 with this Directive. Where appropriate, the competent authorities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 may request the competent authorities under this Directive to exercise their supervisory and enforcement powers in relation to an entity that is identified as a critical entity under Directive (EU) 2022/2557.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive cooperate with
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive cooperate with the relevant competent authorities of the Member State concerned under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. In particular, Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive inform the Oversight Forum established pursuant to Article 32(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 when exercising their supervisory and enforcement powers aimed at ensuring compliance of an essential entity that is designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider pursuant to Article 31 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. with this Directive.

requirements.title: When provided with evidence, indication or information that an important entity allegedly does
requirements.text: When provided with evidence, indication or information that an important entity allegedly does not comply with this Directive, in particular Articles 21 and 23 thereof, Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities take action, where necessary, through ex post supervisory measures. Member States shall ensure that those measures are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, taking into account the circumstances of each individual case.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their supervisory
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their supervisory tasks in relation to important entities, have the power to subject those entities at least to:

requirements.title: On-site inspections and off-site ex post supervision conducted by trained professionals
requirements.text: on-site inspections and off-site ex post supervision conducted by trained professionals;

requirements.title: Targeted security audits carried out by an independent body or a competent authority
requirements.text: targeted security audits carried out by an independent body or a competent authority;

requirements.title: Security scans based on objective, non-discriminatory, fair and transparent risk assessment
requirements.text: security scans based on objective, non-discriminatory, fair and transparent risk assessment criteria, where necessary with the cooperation of the entity concerned;

requirements.title: Requests for information necessary to assess, ex post, the cybersecurity risk-management
requirements.text: requests for information necessary to assess, ex post, the cybersecurity risk-management measures adopted by the entity concerned, including documented cybersecurity policies, as well as compliance with the obligation to submit information to the competent authorities pursuant to Article 27;

requirements.title: Requests to access data, documents and information necessary to carry out their supervisory
requirements.text: requests to access data, documents and information necessary to carry out their supervisory tasks;

requirements.title: Requests for evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies, such as the results of
requirements.text: requests for evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies, such as the results of security audits carried out by a qualified auditor and the respective underlying evidence. The targeted security audits referred to in the first subparagraph, point (b), shall be based on risk assessments conducted by the competent authority or the audited entity, or on other risk-related available information. The results of any targeted security audit shall be made available to the competent authority. The costs of such targeted security audit carried out by an independent body shall be paid by the audited entity, except in duly substantiated cases when the competent authority decides otherwise.

requirements.title: When exercising their powers under paragraph 2, point (d), (e) or (f), the competent authorities
requirements.text: When exercising their powers under paragraph 2, point (d), (e) or (f), the competent authorities shall state the purpose of the request and specify the information requested.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their enforcement
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities, when exercising their enforcement powers in relation to important entities, have the power at least to:

requirements.title: Issue warnings about infringements of this Directive by the entities concerned
requirements.text: issue warnings about infringements of this Directive by the entities concerned;

requirements.title: Adopt binding instructions or an order requiring the entities concerned to remedy the
requirements.text: adopt binding instructions or an order requiring the entities concerned to remedy the deficiencies identified or the infringement of this Directive;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to cease conduct that infringes this Directive and desist from
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to cease conduct that infringes this Directive and desist from repeating that conduct;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to ensure that their cybersecurity risk-management measures comply
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to ensure that their cybersecurity risk-management measures comply with Article 21 or to fulfil the reporting obligations laid down in Article 23, in a specified manner and within a specified period;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to inform the natural or legal persons with regard to which they
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to inform the natural or legal persons with regard to which they provide services or carry out activities which are potentially affected by a significant cyber threat of the nature of the threat, as well as of any possible protective or remedial measures which can be taken by those natural or legal persons in response to that threat;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to implement the recommendations provided as a result of a security
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to implement the recommendations provided as a result of a security audit within a reasonable deadline;

requirements.title: Order the entities concerned to make public aspects of infringements of this Directive in a
requirements.text: order the entities concerned to make public aspects of infringements of this Directive in a specified manner;

requirements.title: Impose, or request the imposition by the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance
requirements.text: impose, or request the imposition by the relevant bodies, courts or tribunals, in accordance with national law, of an administrative fine pursuant to Article 34 in addition to any of the measures referred to in points (a) to (g) of this paragraph.

requirements.title: Article 32(6), (7) and (8) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the supervisory and enforcement
requirements.text: Article 32(6), (7) and (8) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the supervisory and enforcement measures provided for in this Article for important entities.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive cooperate with
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive cooperate with the relevant competent authorities of the Member State concerned under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. In particular, Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities under this Directive inform the Oversight Forum established pursuant to Article 32(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 when exercising their supervisory and enforcement powers aimed at ensuring compliance of an important entity that is designated as a critical ICT third-party service provider pursuant to Article 31 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. with this Directive.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that the administrative fines imposed on essential and important
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that the administrative fines imposed on essential and important entities pursuant to this Article in respect of infringements of this Directive are effective, proportionate and dissuasive, taking into account the circumstances of each individual case.

requirements.title: Administrative fines shall be imposed in addition to any of the measures referred to in Article
requirements.text: Administrative fines shall be imposed in addition to any of the measures referred to in Article 32(4), points (a) to (h), Article 32(5) and Article 33(4), points (a) to (g).

requirements.title: When deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and deciding on its amount in each
requirements.text: When deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and deciding on its amount in each individual case, due regard shall be given, as a minimum, to the elements provided for in Article 32(7).

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that where they infringe Article 21 or 23, essential entities are
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that where they infringe Article 21 or 23, essential entities are subject, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article, to administrative fines of a maximum of at least EUR 10 000 000 or of a maximum of at least 2 % of the total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year of the undertaking to which the essential entity belongs, whichever is higher.

requirements.title: Member States shall ensure that where they infringe Article 21 or 23, important entities are
requirements.text: Member States shall ensure that where they infringe Article 21 or 23, important entities are subject, in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article, to administrative fines of a maximum of at least EUR 7 000 000 or of a maximum of at least 1,4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year of the undertaking to which the important entity belongs, whichever is higher.

requirements.title: Member States may provide for the power to impose periodic penalty payments in order to compel
requirements.text: Member States may provide for the power to impose periodic penalty payments in order to compel an essential or important entity to cease an infringement of this Directive in accordance with a prior decision of the competent authority.

requirements.title: Without prejudice to the powers of the competent authorities pursuant to Articles 32 and 33
requirements.text: Without prejudice to the powers of the competent authorities pursuant to Articles 32 and 33, each Member State may lay down the rules on whether and to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public administration entities.

requirements.title: Where the legal system of a Member State does not provide for administrative fines, that Member
requirements.text: Where the legal system of a Member State does not provide for administrative fines, that Member State shall ensure that this Article is applied in such a manner that the fine is initiated by the competent authority and imposed by competent national courts or tribunals, while ensuring that those legal remedies are effective and have an equivalent effect to the administrative fines imposed by the competent authorities. In any event, the fines imposed shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. The Member State shall notify to the Commission the provisions of the laws which it adopts pursuant to this paragraph by 17 October 2024 and, without delay, any subsequent amendment law or amendment affecting them.

requirements.title: Where the competent authorities become aware in the course of supervision or enforcement that
requirements.text: Where the competent authorities become aware in the course of supervision or enforcement that the infringement by an essential or important entity of the obligations laid down in Articles 21 and 23 of this Directive can entail a personal data breach, as defined in Article 4, point (12), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 which is to be notified pursuant to Article 33 of that Regulation, they shall, without undue delay, inform the supervisory authorities as referred to in Article 55 or 56 of that Regulation.

requirements.title: Where the supervisory authorities as referred to in Article 55 or 56 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
requirements.text: Where the supervisory authorities as referred to in Article 55 or 56 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 impose an administrative fine pursuant to Article 58(2), point (i), of that Regulation, the competent authorities shall not impose an administrative fine pursuant to Article 34 of this Directive for an infringement referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article arising from the same conduct as that which was the subject of the administrative fine under Article 58(2), point (i), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679. The competent authorities may, however, impose the enforcement measures provided for in Article 32(4), points (a) to (h), Article 32(5) and Article 33(4), points (a) to (g), of this Directive.

requirements.title: Where the supervisory authority competent pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 is established in
requirements.text: Where the supervisory authority competent pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2016/679 is established in another Member State than the competent authority, the competent authority shall inform the supervisory authority established in its own Member State of the potential data breach referred to in paragraph 1.

requirements.title: Penalties
requirements.text: Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national measures adopted pursuant to this Directive and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. Member States shall, by 17 January 2025, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures and shall notify it, without delay of any subsequent amendment affecting them.

requirements.title: Where an entity provides services in more than one Member State, or provides services in one or
requirements.text: Where an entity provides services in more than one Member State, or provides services in one or more Member States and its network and information systems are located in one or more other Member States, the competent authorities of the Member States concerned shall cooperate with and assist each other as necessary. That cooperation shall entail, at least, that:

requirements.title: The competent authorities applying supervisory or enforcement measures in a Member State shall
requirements.text: the competent authorities applying supervisory or enforcement measures in a Member State shall, via the single point of contact, inform and consult the competent authorities in the other Member States concerned on the supervisory and enforcement measures taken;

requirements.title: A competent authority may request another competent authority to take supervisory or enforcement
requirements.text: a competent authority may request another competent authority to take supervisory or enforcement measures;

requirements.title: A competent authority shall, upon receipt of a substantiated request from another competent
requirements.text: a competent authority shall, upon receipt of a substantiated request from another competent authority, provide the other competent authority with mutual assistance proportionate to its own resources so that the supervisory or enforcement measures can be implemented in an effective, efficient and consistent manner. The mutual assistance referred to in the first subparagraph, point (c), may cover information requests and supervisory measures, including requests to carry out on-site inspections or off-site supervision or targeted security audits. A competent authority to which a request for assistance is addressed shall not refuse that request unless it is established that it does not have the competence to provide the requested assistance, the requested assistance is not proportionate to the supervisory tasks of the competent authority, or the request concerns information or entails activities which, if disclosed or carried out, would be contrary to the essential interests of the Member State’s national security, public security or defence. Before refusing such a request, the competent authority shall consult the other competent authorities concerned as well as, upon the request of one of the Member States concerned, the Commission and ENISA.

requirements.title: Where appropriate and with common agreement, the competent authorities of various Member States
requirements.text: Where appropriate and with common agreement, the competent authorities of various Member States may carry out joint supervisory actions.

requirements.title: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid
requirements.text: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.

requirements.title: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 24(2) shall be conferred on the
requirements.text: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 24(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 16 January 2023.

requirements.title: The delegation of power referred to in Article 24(2) may be revoked at any time by the European
requirements.text: The delegation of power referred to in Article 24(2) may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision to revoke shall put an end to the delegation of the power specified in that decision. It shall take effect the day following the publication of the decision in the Official Journal of the European Union or at a later date specified therein. It shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.

requirements.title: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member
requirements.text: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles laid down in the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.

requirements.title: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the
requirements.text: As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.

requirements.title: A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 24(2) shall enter into force only if no objection
requirements.text: A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 24(2) shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament or by the Council within a period of two months of notification of that act to the European Parliament and to the Council or if, before the expiry of that period, the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object. That period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.

requirements.title: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee
requirements.text: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

requirements.title: Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply
requirements.text: Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.

requirements.title: Where the opinion of the committee is to be obtained by written procedure, that procedure shall
requirements.text: Where the opinion of the committee is to be obtained by written procedure, that procedure shall be terminated without result when, within the time-limit for delivery of the opinion, the chair of the committee so decides or a committee member so requests.

requirements.title: Review
requirements.text: By 17 October 2027 and every 36 months thereafter, the Commission shall review the functioning of this Directive, and report to the European Parliament and to the Council. The report shall in particular assess the relevance of the size of the entities concerned, and the sectors, subsectors and types of entity referred to in Annexes I and II for the functioning of the economy and society in relation to cybersecurity. To that end and with a view to further advancing the strategic and operational cooperation, the Commission shall take into account the reports of the Cooperation Group and the CSIRTs network on the experience gained at a strategic and operational level. The report shall be accompanied, where necessary, by a legislative proposal.

requirements.title: By 17 October 2024, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with
requirements.text: By 17 October 2024, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. They shall apply those measures from 18 October 2024.

requirements.title: When Member States adopt the measures referred to in paragraph 1, they shall contain a reference
requirements.text: When Member States adopt the measures referred to in paragraph 1, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or shall be accompanied by such reference on the occasion of their official publication. The methods of making such reference shall be laid down by Member States.

requirements.title: Amendment of Regulation (EU) No 910/2014
requirements.text: In Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, Article 19 is deleted with effect from 18 October 2024.

requirements.title: Amendment of Directive (EU) 2018/1972
requirements.text: In Directive (EU) 2018/1972, Articles 40 and 41 are deleted with effect from 18 October 2024.

requirements.title: Repeal
requirements.text: Directive (EU) 2016/1148 is repealed with effect from 18 October 2024.

requirements.title: Entry into force
requirements.text: This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

requirements.title: Addressees
requirements.text: This Directive is addressed to the Member States.

requirements.title: Policies for information security
requirements.text: Maintain a current information security policy approved at management level. Evidence: signed policy, approval record, and review date.

requirements.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
requirements.text: Define security roles and assign responsibilities across the organization, including deputies. Evidence: role matrix, job descriptions, and appointment records.

requirements.title: Segregation of duties
requirements.text: Separate conflicting duties so one person cannot both initiate and approve a sensitive action. Evidence: role matrix and access review records.

requirements.title: Management responsibilities
requirements.text: Require staff to apply the information security policy and hold managers accountable for compliance in their area. Evidence: management communications and performance objectives.

requirements.title: Contact with authorities
requirements.text: Keep current contacts for regulators, law enforcement, and incident response bodies. Evidence: contact list and records of past notifications.

requirements.title: Contact with special interest groups
requirements.text: Maintain memberships and contacts with security communities and industry groups. Evidence: membership records and meeting notes.

requirements.title: Threat intelligence
requirements.text: Collect and use threat intelligence to inform risk decisions and control priorities. Evidence: threat reports, subscriptions, and action logs.

requirements.title: Information security in project management
requirements.text: Integrate information security requirements into project planning and delivery gates. Evidence: project charters, risk assessments, and gate reviews.

requirements.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
requirements.text: Keep an inventory of information and related assets with named owners. Evidence: asset register, ownership field, and periodic reconciliation.

requirements.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
requirements.text: Publish rules for acceptable use of information and assets and confirm that staff acknowledge them. Evidence: acceptable use policy and acknowledgements.

requirements.title: Return of assets
requirements.text: Require return of assets when employment or a contract ends. Evidence: exit checklists and asset return receipts.

requirements.title: Classification of information
requirements.text: Classify information by sensitivity and handling needs, and keep the scheme current. Evidence: classification policy, scheme, and tagged assets.

requirements.title: Labelling of information
requirements.text: Apply consistent labels so users can recognize sensitivity and handling rules. Evidence: labelling standard and examples from systems.

requirements.title: Information transfer
requirements.text: Protect information in transit through approved channels, agreements, and transfer rules. Evidence: transfer procedures and secure channel configuration.

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.text: Define access control rules based on business and security requirements. Evidence: access control policy and authorization records.

requirements.title: Identity management
requirements.text: Manage identities through a controlled lifecycle from creation to removal. Evidence: identity register and joiner, mover, and leaver records.

requirements.title: Authentication information
requirements.text: Control issuance, storage, and rotation of authentication secrets. Evidence: password policy, multi-factor configuration, and secret rotation logs.

requirements.title: Access rights
requirements.text: Grant, review, and revoke access rights according to approved roles and least privilege. Evidence: access approvals and periodic review reports.

requirements.title: Information security in supplier relationships
requirements.text: Assess security risks in supplier relationships before and during the engagement. Evidence: supplier risk assessments and due diligence records.

requirements.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
requirements.text: Include information security duties and expectations in supplier agreements. Evidence: contract clauses, security schedules, and signed agreements.

requirements.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
requirements.text: Manage ICT supply chain risks, including sub-suppliers and component provenance. Evidence: supply chain map, supplier attestations, and review notes.

requirements.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
requirements.text: Monitor supplier service performance and security changes, and review them periodically. Evidence: service reports, change notices, and review minutes.

requirements.title: Information security for use of cloud services
requirements.text: Define security requirements and responsibilities for cloud service use. Evidence: cloud inventory, provider contracts, and configuration reviews.

requirements.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
requirements.text: Plan and prepare incident management, including roles, channels, and escalation paths. Evidence: incident plan, contact list, and exercise records.

requirements.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
requirements.text: Triage security events consistently and record the decision to escalate or close them. Evidence: triage records and event classification criteria.

requirements.title: Response to information security incidents
requirements.text: Respond to incidents through the documented process and preserve the response record. Evidence: incident tickets, timelines, and closure reports.

requirements.title: Learning from information security incidents
requirements.text: Review incidents to identify root causes and improve controls. Evidence: post-incident reviews and tracked corrective actions.

requirements.title: Collection of evidence
requirements.text: Collect and preserve incident evidence using defensible methods. Evidence: evidence register, chain of custody, and hash records.

requirements.title: Information security during disruption
requirements.text: Keep security controls operating during disruption and document degraded-mode procedures. Evidence: continuity plan and disruption test results.

requirements.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
requirements.text: Define and test ICT recovery capability against agreed objectives. Evidence: recovery plan, recovery targets, and exercise reports.

requirements.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
requirements.text: Identify and track legal, regulatory, and contractual security obligations. Evidence: obligations register, legal review, and compliance calendar.

requirements.title: Intellectual property rights
requirements.text: Protect intellectual property and ensure software licences are used lawfully. Evidence: licence inventory and software asset records.

requirements.title: Protection of records
requirements.text: Protect records from loss, alteration, and unauthorized access for the required period. Evidence: retention schedule and storage controls.

requirements.title: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
requirements.text: Identify and protect personal data in line with privacy obligations. Evidence: data inventory, privacy notices, and handling procedures.

requirements.title: Independent review of information security
requirements.text: Obtain independent review of the security management system at planned intervals. Evidence: audit reports and management responses.

requirements.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
requirements.text: Review compliance with internal security rules and record exceptions. Evidence: compliance checks, exception register, and remediation plans.

requirements.title: Documented operating procedures
requirements.text: Document operating procedures for security-relevant tasks and keep them available to staff. Evidence: procedure library, version history, and acknowledgements.

requirements.title: Screening
requirements.text: Screen candidates before employment and repeat checks where the role requires it. Evidence: screening policy and completed check records.

requirements.title: Terms and conditions of employment
requirements.text: State security responsibilities and confidentiality duties in employment terms. Evidence: employment contracts and role descriptions.

requirements.title: Information security awareness, education and training
requirements.text: Provide role-appropriate security awareness and training, and track completion. Evidence: training plan, attendance, and assessment results.

requirements.title: Disciplinary process
requirements.text: Apply a documented disciplinary process for security policy violations. Evidence: disciplinary procedure, case records, and HR notifications.

requirements.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
requirements.text: Define security duties that continue or end when employment changes or terminates. Evidence: exit procedure and acknowledgement records.

requirements.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
requirements.text: Use confidentiality agreements that cover employees, contractors, and relevant third parties. Evidence: signed agreements and contract templates.

requirements.title: Remote working
requirements.text: Set security requirements for remote work, including devices, networks, and physical privacy. Evidence: remote work policy and device compliance reports.

requirements.title: Information security event reporting
requirements.text: Give staff a simple route to report security events and confirm that reports are handled. Evidence: reporting channel, awareness material, and report log.

requirements.title: Physical security perimeters
requirements.text: Define physical security perimeters that protect information processing facilities. Evidence: site plan, perimeter controls, and inspection records.

requirements.title: Physical entry
requirements.text: Control entry to secure areas through badges, reception, or other approved mechanisms. Evidence: access logs, visitor records, and entry procedures.

requirements.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
requirements.text: Design and protect offices, rooms, and facilities against unauthorized access and damage. Evidence: facility standards, risk assessments, and inspection reports.

requirements.title: Physical security monitoring
requirements.text: Monitor physical premises for unauthorized access and suspicious activity. Evidence: camera retention settings, alarm logs, and response records.

requirements.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
requirements.text: Protect facilities from environmental and physical threats such as fire, flood, and power loss. Evidence: risk assessment and protection system test records.

requirements.title: Working in secure areas
requirements.text: Restrict work in secure areas and supervise or escort visitors. Evidence: secure area rules, access lists, and visitor logs.

requirements.title: Clear desk and clear screen
requirements.text: Require staff to secure information and devices when leaving a workspace. Evidence: clear desk policy and spot-check results.

requirements.title: Equipment siting and protection
requirements.text: Site and protect equipment to reduce environmental and unauthorized-access risk. Evidence: equipment placement standards and site inspections.

requirements.title: Security of assets off-premises
requirements.text: Protect assets used outside the premises, including travel and home use. Evidence: off-site asset register and device protection records.

requirements.title: Storage media
requirements.text: Manage storage media through labelling, secure storage, transport, and disposal. Evidence: media register, transfer logs, and destruction certificates.

requirements.title: Supporting utilities
requirements.text: Provide and test supporting utilities that information processing depends on. Evidence: utility inventory, maintenance records, and failover tests.

requirements.title: Cabling security
requirements.text: Protect power and communication cabling from interception, interference, and damage. Evidence: cabling standards and installation inspection records.

requirements.title: Equipment maintenance
requirements.text: Maintain equipment according to manufacturer guidance and record the work. Evidence: maintenance schedule, service reports, and asset history.

requirements.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
requirements.text: Sanitize or destroy equipment and storage media before disposal or reuse. Evidence: disposal procedure and certificates of destruction.

requirements.title: User endpoint devices
requirements.text: Apply configuration and protection standards to user endpoint devices. Evidence: device baseline, compliance reports, and exception list.

requirements.title: Privileged access rights
requirements.text: Limit and monitor privileged access rights, and review them regularly. Evidence: privileged account inventory and review records.

requirements.title: Information access restriction
requirements.text: Restrict access to information and functions according to defined policy. Evidence: access matrix, permission exports, and approvals.

requirements.title: Access to source code
requirements.text: Control read and write access to source code and development artefacts. Evidence: repository permissions and code review records.

requirements.title: Secure authentication
requirements.text: Use secure authentication methods appropriate to the risk, including multi-factor authentication where needed. Evidence: authentication configuration and enforcement reports.

requirements.title: Capacity management
requirements.text: Monitor capacity and plan resources to meet performance and availability needs. Evidence: capacity reports, thresholds, and scaling records.

requirements.title: Protection against malware
requirements.text: Deploy malware protection and keep detection content current. Evidence: endpoint protection console and update compliance reports.

requirements.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
requirements.text: Identify, prioritize, and remediate technical vulnerabilities within defined timelines. Evidence: scan results, patch records, and remediation tickets.

requirements.title: Configuration management
requirements.text: Establish and maintain secure configuration baselines for systems and services. Evidence: hardened images, configuration exports, and drift alerts.

requirements.title: Information deletion
requirements.text: Delete information when it is no longer required and verify deletion where promised. Evidence: retention schedule and deletion records.

requirements.title: Data masking
requirements.text: Mask sensitive data in non-production and lower-trust contexts. Evidence: masking rules and sample test results.

requirements.title: Data leakage prevention
requirements.text: Prevent unauthorized extraction of sensitive information through technical and procedural controls. Evidence: data loss prevention rules, alerts, and investigation records.

requirements.title: Information backup
requirements.text: Back up information and test restoration against agreed objectives. Evidence: backup schedule, restore tests, and failure records.

requirements.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
requirements.text: Provide redundancy for information processing facilities where availability requires it. Evidence: architecture diagram, failover tests, and uptime reports.

requirements.title: Logging
requirements.text: Produce and protect logs that support detection, investigation, and audit. Evidence: logging standard, retention settings, and sample logs.

requirements.title: Monitoring activities
requirements.text: Monitor systems and networks for anomalous behavior and follow up on alerts. Evidence: monitoring dashboards, alert tickets, and tuning records.

requirements.title: Clock synchronization
requirements.text: Synchronize system clocks to an approved time source. Evidence: time source configuration and drift monitoring reports.

requirements.title: Use of privileged utility programs
requirements.text: Restrict and log use of utility programs that can bypass controls. Evidence: utility inventory, approvals, and command logs.

requirements.title: Installation of software on operational systems
requirements.text: Control installation of software on operational systems through approval and verification. Evidence: software catalogue, installation records, and change tickets.

requirements.title: Networks security
requirements.text: Protect networks through segmentation, secure configuration, and monitoring. Evidence: network diagrams, firewall rules, and review records.

requirements.title: Security of network services
requirements.text: Define security requirements for network services and verify that they are met. Evidence: service specifications, configuration baselines, and test results.

requirements.title: Segregation of networks
requirements.text: Separate networks by trust level and business function. Evidence: network zones, segmentation rules, and connectivity tests.

requirements.title: Web filtering
requirements.text: Filter access to external websites to reduce malware and data-loss risk. Evidence: web filter policy and blocked-request reports.

requirements.title: Use of cryptography
requirements.text: Define when and how cryptography is used, including key management. Evidence: cryptography policy, key inventory, and algorithm standards.

requirements.title: Secure development life cycle
requirements.text: Embed security activities into each stage of the development lifecycle. Evidence: development lifecycle definition, security gates, and project records.

requirements.title: Application security requirements
requirements.text: Specify security requirements for applications and verify them before release. Evidence: requirements backlog, threat model, and acceptance tests.

requirements.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
requirements.text: Apply secure architecture and engineering principles to systems and services. Evidence: architecture standards, design reviews, and exceptions.

requirements.title: Secure coding
requirements.text: Set secure coding standards and verify them through review and tooling. Evidence: coding standard, code review records, and scanner results.

requirements.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
requirements.text: Test security in development and acceptance before changes reach production. Evidence: test plans, penetration test reports, and defect records.

requirements.title: Outsourced development
requirements.text: Apply the same security expectations to outsourced development and verify delivery. Evidence: supplier requirements, code review records, and acceptance tests.

requirements.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
requirements.text: Keep development, test, and production environments separated and controlled. Evidence: environment inventory, access controls, and data-flow review.

requirements.title: Change management
requirements.text: Manage changes through request, assessment, approval, testing, and rollback planning. Evidence: change tickets, approvals, and post-implementation reviews.

requirements.title: Test information
requirements.text: Protect test information and prefer synthetic data over production data. Evidence: test data policy and data generation records.

requirements.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
requirements.text: Protect systems and data during audit testing and agree the scope in advance. Evidence: audit plan, access approvals, and test logs.

requirements.title: Integrity and ethical values
requirements.text: Set expectations for ethical conduct and communicate them to staff and contractors. Evidence: code of conduct, acknowledgements, and investigation records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC1.1

requirements.title: Board oversight
requirements.text: Provide independent oversight of internal control over security. Evidence: board or committee charter, minutes, and oversight reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC1.2

requirements.title: Management structure and authority
requirements.text: Define reporting lines, authority, and responsibilities for security work. Evidence: organization chart, delegations, and role descriptions.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC1.3

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.text: Require the skills needed for security roles and support their development. Evidence: job requirements, training records, and performance reviews.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC1.4

requirements.title: Accountability
requirements.text: Hold individuals accountable for security responsibilities and measure performance. Evidence: objectives, performance reviews, and corrective actions.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC1.5

requirements.title: Quality information
requirements.text: Use relevant and accurate information to operate and monitor security controls. Evidence: data sources, quality checks, and management reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC2.1

requirements.title: Internal communication
requirements.text: Communicate security responsibilities and expectations across the organization. Evidence: policies, briefings, and acknowledgement records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC2.2

requirements.title: External communication
requirements.text: Communicate with customers, partners, and regulators about security matters as required. Evidence: communication channels, notices, and inquiry logs.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC2.3

requirements.title: Objectives and risk identification
requirements.text: Define security objectives and identify risks that could prevent their achievement. Evidence: objectives, risk register, and assessment records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC3.1

requirements.title: Risk analysis
requirements.text: Analyze identified risks for likelihood and impact, and decide how to respond. Evidence: risk scoring method, risk register, and treatment plans.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC3.2

requirements.title: Fraud risk
requirements.text: Consider the potential for fraud when assessing risks to security objectives. Evidence: fraud risk assessment and management review.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC3.3

requirements.title: Changes in risk
requirements.text: Reassess risk when the business, technology, or threat environment changes. Evidence: change impact assessments and updated risk records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC3.4

requirements.title: Ongoing and separate evaluations
requirements.text: Evaluate controls through continuous monitoring and periodic independent reviews. Evidence: monitoring reports, internal audit results, and test scripts.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC4.1

requirements.title: Communication of deficiencies
requirements.text: Report control deficiencies to those responsible and track remediation. Evidence: issue register, remediation plans, and closure evidence.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC4.2

requirements.title: Control activities selection
requirements.text: Select controls that mitigate the risks identified for security objectives. Evidence: control matrix and risk-to-control mapping.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC5.1

requirements.title: Technology general controls
requirements.text: Rely on properly designed and operating technology controls, including infrastructure and processes. Evidence: technology control test results and system inventories.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC5.2

requirements.title: Policies and procedures
requirements.text: Document policies and procedures and keep them current and available. Evidence: policy library, version history, and review approvals.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC5.3

requirements.title: Logical access security
requirements.text: Protect systems and data with logical access controls across software, infrastructure, and architecture. Evidence: access control design, identity configuration, and test results.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.1

requirements.title: User registration and authorization
requirements.text: Register and authorize new internal and external users before access is granted. Evidence: onboarding tickets, approvals, and user listings.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.2

requirements.title: Role-based access and least privilege
requirements.text: Assign access by role and limit it to what the role requires. Evidence: role definitions, entitlement mappings, and access reviews.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.3

requirements.title: Physical access to facilities
requirements.text: Restrict physical access to facilities that host or support systems and data. Evidence: badge lists, visitor logs, and access reviews.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.4

requirements.title: Access removal
requirements.text: Remove logical and physical access promptly when people leave or change roles. Evidence: termination tickets, deprovisioning logs, and badge returns.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.5

requirements.title: External threats
requirements.text: Protect against threats that originate outside the system boundary. Evidence: boundary diagram, firewall rules, and intrusion alerts.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.6

requirements.title: Information transmission and removal
requirements.text: Restrict transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorized channels. Evidence: transfer policy, encryption settings, and exception approvals.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.7

requirements.title: Malicious software
requirements.text: Prevent, detect, and respond to unauthorized or malicious software. Evidence: endpoint controls, application allowlists, and malware alerts.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC6.8

requirements.title: Configuration and vulnerability management
requirements.text: Detect configuration drift and vulnerabilities, and correct them on a defined schedule. Evidence: baselines, scans, and remediation records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC7.1

requirements.title: Monitoring
requirements.text: Monitor system components for anomalies that indicate security incidents. Evidence: monitoring coverage, alert rules, and response tickets.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC7.2

requirements.title: Incident identification
requirements.text: Evaluate security events to decide whether they are incidents and assign severity. Evidence: triage records, severity guide, and incident log.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC7.3

requirements.title: Incident response
requirements.text: Execute the incident response plan and communicate with affected parties. Evidence: incident plans, response timelines, and communications.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC7.4

requirements.title: Incident recovery
requirements.text: Recover from incidents and confirm that systems and data are restored correctly. Evidence: recovery plans, restoration tests, and closure reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC7.5

requirements.title: Change management
requirements.text: Authorize, design, test, approve, and implement changes through a controlled process. Evidence: change tickets, approvals, test results, and deployment logs.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC8.1

requirements.title: Risk mitigation
requirements.text: Identify and implement mitigation for business disruption and security risks. Evidence: risk treatment plans, insurance, and continuity arrangements.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC9.1

requirements.title: Vendor risk management
requirements.text: Assess and monitor vendors and business partners that could affect security objectives. Evidence: vendor inventory, due diligence, and contract reviews.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), CC9.2

requirements.title: Capacity management
requirements.text: Monitor and manage capacity so systems meet availability commitments. Evidence: capacity plans, utilization reports, and scaling records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), A1.1

requirements.title: Backup and recovery
requirements.text: Maintain backups and recovery arrangements that meet availability objectives. Evidence: backup schedules, off-site copies, and restore test reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), A1.2

requirements.title: Recovery testing
requirements.text: Test recovery plans periodically and correct failures found in exercises. Evidence: exercise plans, results, and follow-up actions.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), A1.3

requirements.title: Processing objectives
requirements.text: Define what complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized processing means for the service. Evidence: processing objectives and service specifications.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), PI1.1

requirements.title: Input controls
requirements.text: Validate inputs so processing uses complete and accurate data. Evidence: input validation rules, error reports, and reconciliation.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), PI1.2

requirements.title: Processing controls
requirements.text: Monitor processing for errors and exceptions, and resolve them. Evidence: job monitoring, exception queues, and correction records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), PI1.3

requirements.title: Output controls
requirements.text: Verify that outputs are complete, accurate, and delivered to authorized recipients. Evidence: output reconciliation and distribution records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), PI1.4

requirements.title: Stored data integrity
requirements.text: Protect stored data from unauthorized or accidental alteration and loss. Evidence: integrity checks, access controls, and restore records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), PI1.5

requirements.title: Confidentiality identification and retention
requirements.text: Identify confidential information and retain it only as long as needed. Evidence: data inventory, retention schedule, and disposal records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), C1.1

requirements.title: Confidentiality disposal
requirements.text: Dispose of confidential information securely when it is no longer required. Evidence: disposal procedure and destruction certificates.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), C1.2

requirements.title: Privacy notice
requirements.text: Tell data subjects what personal information is collected and how it is used. Evidence: privacy notice, publication record, and change history.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P1.1

requirements.title: Choice and consent
requirements.text: Offer and record choices about the collection, use, retention, and disclosure of personal information. Evidence: consent flows and consent records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P2.1

requirements.title: Collection limited to objectives
requirements.text: Collect personal information only for the purposes described in the notice. Evidence: data inventory and collection-point review.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P3.1

requirements.title: Lawful and fair collection
requirements.text: Collect personal information by lawful and fair means. Evidence: collection procedures and legal basis records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P3.2

requirements.title: Use limited to objectives
requirements.text: Use personal information only for identified purposes and any consent obtained. Evidence: purpose mapping and access review records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P4.1

requirements.title: Retention
requirements.text: Retain personal information only as long as the stated objectives require. Evidence: retention schedule and purge reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P4.2

requirements.title: Disposal
requirements.text: Dispose of personal information securely when retention ends. Evidence: disposal procedure and destruction logs.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P4.3

requirements.title: Access by data subjects
requirements.text: Let authenticated data subjects access their personal information and learn whether it is held. Evidence: request workflow and response records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P5.1

requirements.title: Correction
requirements.text: Correct, amend, or append personal information on request and notify relevant third parties. Evidence: correction requests and propagation records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P5.2

requirements.title: Disclosure with consent
requirements.text: Disclose personal information to third parties only with consent or another stated basis. Evidence: disclosure register and consent records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.1

requirements.title: Authorized disclosure records
requirements.text: Keep complete and accurate records of authorized disclosures. Evidence: disclosure log and reconciliation.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.2

requirements.title: Unauthorized disclosure records
requirements.text: Record detected or reported unauthorized disclosures and their handling. Evidence: incident register and breach investigation files.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.3

requirements.title: Vendor privacy commitments
requirements.text: Obtain privacy commitments from vendors and other third parties that handle personal information. Evidence: contract clauses and vendor assessments.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.4

requirements.title: Vendor breach notification
requirements.text: Require vendors to notify the organization of actual or suspected unauthorized disclosures. Evidence: contract terms and notification test records.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.5

requirements.title: Breach notification
requirements.text: Notify affected data subjects, regulators, and others when a breach requires it. Evidence: notification procedure and breach notices.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.6

requirements.title: Accounting of disclosures
requirements.text: Provide data subjects with an accounting of personal information held and disclosed. Evidence: request workflow and disclosure reports.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P6.7

requirements.title: Data quality
requirements.text: Keep personal information accurate, current, and complete for its intended use. Evidence: quality checks, correction requests, and reconciliation.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P7.1

requirements.title: Privacy monitoring and enforcement
requirements.text: Monitor privacy compliance, handle complaints, and apply consequences for violations. Evidence: complaint log, investigation records, and disciplinary actions.
requirements.sourceRef: AICPA Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised 2022), P8.1
